{{Short description|American mathematician (1935–2017)}}
{{distinguish|text=[[Martin Greenberg (disambiguation)|Martin Greenberg]]}}

[[File:Marvin Greenberg.jpg|thumb|Marvin Greenberg at [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]] in 1975]]
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2017}}
'''Marvin Jay Greenberg''' (December 22, 1935 – December 12, 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2017/12/greenberg-in-memoriam.html|title=In Memoriam: Marvin Greenberg (1935–2017)|website=UC Santa Cruz Newscenter|access-date=December 16, 2017|archive-date=April 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410051904/https://news.ucsc.edu/2017/12/greenberg-in-memoriam.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>) was an American mathematician.

== Education ==
Greenberg studied at [[Columbia University]] where he received his bachelor's degree in 1955 (he was a Ford Scholar as an undergraduate) and received his doctorate 1959 from [[Princeton University]] under [[Serge Lang]] with the thesis ''Pro-Algebraic Structure on the Rational Subgroup of a P-Adic Abelian Variety''.

== Career ==
From 1955 Greenberg was an assistant at Princeton, from 1958 an assistant at the [[University of Chicago]] and in 1958 and 1959, an instructor at [[Rutgers University]]. From 1959 to 1964 he was an assistant professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], two years of which time he spent on [[National Science Foundation]] postdoctoral fellowships at [[Harvard University]] and the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] in [[Paris]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://macmillanlearning.com/Catalog/Author/marvinjgreenberg|title=Marvin J. Greenberg|website=macmillanlearning.com|language=en|access-date=December 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219182340/https://www.macmillanlearning.com/Catalog/Author/marvinjgreenberg|archive-date=December 19, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

From 1965 to 1967 he was an associate professor at [[Northeastern University]] and from 1967 he worked as an associate professor, and later full professor, at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]]. He retired early in 1992 and moved back to Berkeley.

He was known for his book on [[non-Euclidean geometry]] (1st edition, 1974; 4th edition, 2008)<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uCYPZ4nRqy0C | title=Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries: Development and History | isbn=978-0-7167-2446-9 | last1=Greenberg | first1=Marvin J. | date=15 July 1993 | edition=3rd |publisher=Macmillan }} {{cite book| title=2nd edition | isbn=978-0-7167-1103-2 | date=1980 | publisher=W. H. Freeman }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Boman, Eugene|title=Review of ''Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries: Development and History'' by Marvin J. Greenberg|journal=Convergence|date=April 2010}}; Boman's review reprinted in: {{cite web|url=https://old.maa.org/press/periodicals/convergence/euclidean-and-non-euclidean-geometries-development-and-history |title=Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries: Development and History &#124; Mathematical Association of America }}</ref> and his book on [[algebraic topology]] (1st edition, 1967, published with the title ''Lectures on Algebraic Topology''; revised edition published, with John R. Harper as co-author, in 1981 with the title ''Algebraic Topology: A First Course'').<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KlHvAAAAMAAJ | title=Lectures on Algebraic Topology | isbn=978-0-8053-3554-5 | last1=Greenberg | first1=Marvin J. | date=1967 | publisher=W. A. Benjamin }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LmhQDwAAQBAJ | title=Algebraic Topology: A First Course | isbn=978-0-429-97095-5 | last1=Greenberg | first1=Marvin J. |author2=Harper, John R.| date=5 March 2018 | publisher=CRC Press |postscript=; pbk reprint of 1981 edition}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.2307/3615551|jstor=3615551 |last1=Griffiths |first1=H. B. |title=Reviewed work: ''Algebraic Topology, a First Course'', Marvin J. Greenberg, John R. Harper |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |date=1982 |volume=66 |issue=438 |pages=337–338 }}</ref>

Greenberg was also a passionate golfer and a founding member of the Shivas Irons Society.
